findings.stat_label: monthly maintenance fee, yours vs peer median
findings.headline: Your monthly maintenance fee is well above the market range.
findings.body: At $10, it is 2× the $5 peer median and the 87th percentile of 23 peers (middle half of the market: $4.50–$7.50). Maintenance fees are the line account shoppers compare first, before any penalty fee.

findings.headline: Several lines are priced below the market.
findings.body: Your NSF / returned-item fee ($20 vs a $27.75 median) and cashier's check fee ($2 vs a $5 median) each sit below the peer 25th percentile. Below-market returned-item pricing is a position many institutions are moving toward. If the pricing is deliberate, it is worth stating plainly in account marketing.

findings.stat_label: comparable lines inside the market range
findings.headline: Most of your schedule is priced with the market.
findings.body: Of the 8 fee lines where we found both your published amount and at least eight comparable peers, five sit between the peer 25th and 75th percentiles, one above and two below.

exec_narrative: Emblem Credit Union is compared with 141 credit unions under $10B in assets nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index. The size band is wider than usual because fewer than 40 credit unions in your own size tier have published data; local competitors may price differently. Of 8 rankable lines, five sit inside the middle half of the market, one above it (monthly maintenance fee), and two below it (NSF / returned-item fee and cashier's check fee). We would suggest three steps, in order of value: (1) review the monthly maintenance fee, which sits well above the market range; the peer median of $5 is the reference point; (2) state the below-market NSF / returned-item fee in account marketing, where peers' published schedules make it verifiable; (3) check that the non-network ATM and overdraft fees are published where customers can find them.

callouts.title: Monthly maintenance fee — $10
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $4.50–$7.50 · range $0–$25 · 87th percentile · n=23
callouts.body: Published as “Monthly Service Fee.” At $10 it is 2× the $5 peer median. Maintenance fees are the line account shoppers compare first, before any penalty fee. If the account carries waivers, the waiver terms matter more than the headline price; make sure they are as visible as the fee.

callouts.title: NSF / returned-item fee — $20
callouts.stat: Peer median $27.75 · middle half $23–$30 · 25th percentile · n=60
callouts.body: Published as “Insufficient Funds.” Below-market returned-item pricing is a position many institutions are moving toward. If it is a deliberate choice, it belongs in account marketing; if it is an old price that was never revisited, the median of $27.75 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Cashier's check fee — $2
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $3–$5 · 21st percentile · n=29
callouts.body: Published as “Cashier's Checks.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $5 is the reference point.

callouts.body: Absence here means the line was not in the documents listed in § 06, not that you do not charge it. Regulators and comparison sites increasingly expect the full consumer fee schedule to be posted in one place.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Emblem Credit Union with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
